column3: “This is” supplies the nominal sentence’s verb.
BSB’s “Behold” matches the Textus Receptus (ἰδοὺ); the critical text lacks it. “Will send” renders the present “I send.”
“People ... from” makes the inhabitants explicit; the confession is moved earlier.
Eating is replaced by a statement about His food.
The present coming is expressed in the future.
“Jesus” makes the pronoun explicit; the historical present becomes past.
“Jesus” makes the subject explicit; Simon’s repeated name is replaced by “his.”
“Jesus and His companions” makes “they” explicit; “began” is supplied.
The man’s being there and crying are combined.
“What do You want with us” interprets the idiom.
“Jesus and His companions” makes the subject explicit.
“Jesus” makes the pronoun explicit; the historical present becomes past.
